My family has farmed this land for generations. I have about 10 mu — all on the flat plain, good loamy soil. My husband works construction in Handan city during slack periods, so I run most of the farm myself. I know one system well: wheat in winter, corn in summer, on the same fields. That is what I will do again.

For wheat, I will plant in early October after the corn harvest. I will hire the neighbor's rotary tiller — we always rotary-till before wheat, it's faster and easier. I buy the improved wheat variety from the township seed shop, the same one I used last three years — Jimai 22 or whatever they have this year from the same family. Fertilizer: I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then urea at jointing. I water three times: the winter irrigation in November, once at jointing in April, once near heading in May. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew — two times usually, sometimes three if the spring is wet. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe a bit more.

For corn, I plant immediately after the wheat harvest in early June — I plant directly into the stubble, no tilling, saves time and money. I use hybrid seed, the kind the seed shop pushes, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335. I split the fertilizer — some compound at planting, urea applied by hand around knee-height. Summer usually brings enough rain, but I water once or twice if July is dry. I spray once for corn borer. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

I will not try vegetables or cotton — I don't have the connections to sell them, and the price is unpredictable. Wheat and corn I can sell to the grain station. It is steady.
